buildNotes: Every seesaw access is a write of two bytes, module base then function register; for a read wait a few ms, then read the bytes back, big-endian.

Keys A-D are seesaw pins 4-7: set them input with pull-up (DIRCLR_BULK 0x01 0x03, PULLENSET 0x01 0x0B, BULK_SET 0x01 0x05, mask 0xF0), then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); a bit reads 0 while its key is pressed.
NeoPixels: base 0x0E, PIN 0x01 = 3, SPEED 0x02 = 1, BUF_LENGTH 0x03 = 12, BUF 0x04 = 2-byte offset + GRB bytes, SHOW 0x05.
Default address 0x30; close A0/A1/A2/A3 on the back to add 1/2/4/8 (up to 0x3F).
Key switches are not included: plug any Cherry MX-compatible switch into the hot-swap sockets.
Each NeoPixel can draw about 60 mA at full white; keep brightness low on a 3V3 supply.

driver.code:
# Adafruit NeoKey 1x4 QT I2C (product 4980, ATSAMD09 running seesaw firmware), MicroPython driver.
# seesaw protocol: every access starts with a write of [module base, function register];
# for a read, wait briefly, then read the bytes back (all values big-endian).
import time

_STATUS_BASE = 0x00
_STATUS_HW_ID = 0x01
_STATUS_SWRST = 0x7F
_GPIO_BASE = 0x01
_GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK = 0x03
_GPIO_BULK = 0x04
_GPIO_BULK_SET = 0x05
_GPIO_INTENSET = 0x08
_GPIO_INTENCLR = 0x09
_GPIO_PULLENSET = 0x0B
_NEOPIXEL_BASE = 0x0E
_NEOPIXEL_PIN = 0x01
_NEOPIXEL_SPEED = 0x02
_NEOPIXEL_BUF_LENGTH = 0x03
_NEOPIXEL_BUF = 0x04
_NEOPIXEL_SHOW = 0x05

_HW_IDS = (0x55, 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, 0x88, 0x89)  # SAMD09 (this board) and ATtiny8xx/16xx seesaw chips
_KEY_MASK = 0xF0       # keys A-D are seesaw pins 4-7 (PA04-PA07), pressed = pulled to GND
_NEOPIXEL_SEESAW_PIN = 3  # PA03 drives the 4 WS2812B through a 74AHCT1G125 buffer
_NUM_KEYS = 4


class NeoKey1x4:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x30, reset=True, interrupt=False):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            self._write(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_SWRST, b'\xff')
            time.sleep_ms(500)  # seesaw restarts after a software reset
        hw = self._read(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_HW_ID, 1)[0]
        if hw not in _HW_IDS:
            raise OSError('seesaw not found at 0x%02x (HW_ID 0x%02x): check the wiring' % (addr, hw))
        # Keys: inputs with pull-ups (a pressed key shorts the pin to GND).
        mask = _KEY_MASK.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_PULLENSET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK_SET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_INTENSET if interrupt else _GPIO_INTENCLR, mask)
        # NeoPixels: pin 3, 800 kHz, 4 pixels x 3 bytes (GRB).
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_PIN, bytes([_NEOPIXEL_SEESAW_PIN]))
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_SPEED, b'\x01')
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_BUF_LENGTH, (_NUM_KEYS * 3).to_bytes(2, 'big'))

    def _write(self, base, reg, data=b''):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]) + bytes(data))

    def _read(self, base, reg, n, delay_us=8000):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]))
        time.sleep_us(delay_us)  # seesaw needs time to fetch the value before the read
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def keys(self):
        """List of 4 booleans, True while key A, B, C, D (seesaw pins 4-7) is pressed."""
        b = self._read(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK, 4)
        bits = (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]
        return [not (bits >> (4 + i)) & 1 for i in range(_NUM_KEYS)]

    def __getitem__(self, i):
        return self.keys()[i]

    def pixel(self, i, r, g, b, show=True):
        """Set the NeoPixel under key i (0-3) to r, g, b (0-255 each)."""
        if not 0 <= i < _NUM_KEYS:
            raise IndexError('key index 0-3')
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_BUF, (i * 3).to_bytes(2, 'big') + bytes([g & 255, r & 255, b & 255]))
        if show:
            self.show()

    def fill(self, r, g, b):
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_BUF, b'\x00\x00' + bytes([g & 255, r & 255, b & 255]) * _NUM_KEYS)
        self.show()

    def show(self):
        self._write(_NEOPIXEL_BASE, _NEOPIXEL_SHOW)

# Adafruit NeoKey 1x4 QT I2C (Adafruit 4980)

## Overview
A strip of four hot-swap (Kailh) sockets for Cherry MX-compatible key switches, each with a WS2812B RGB NeoPixel under it. An **ATSAMD09D14** running Adafruit's **seesaw** firmware reads the keys and drives the NeoPixels, so the whole board needs only SDA and SCL. It has two STEMMA QT / Qwiic sockets, a 3.3 V regulator (AP2112K) and BSS138 level shifters on the I2C lines. Key switches are sold separately.

## Pinout (header order, as printed on the board)
The 6-pin header appears twice (along both long edges, same signals), so the board does not sit in a breadboard as a single row: wire it with jumper leads to one header or with a STEMMA QT cable. Silkscreen labels, from pin 1:

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3-5 V (use your board's logic voltage); also powers the NeoPixels |
| 3 | 3.3 V regulator output, up to 100 mA (leave unconnected) |
| - | Ground |
| C | I2C clock (SCL), 10 k pull-up to VIN, level-shifted |
| D | I2C data (SDA), 10 k pull-up to VIN, level-shifted |
| INT | seesaw interrupt output, goes low on a key change (only when enabled) |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 3-5 V on VIN. The SAMD09 runs from the on-board 3.3 V regulator.
- I2C is level-shifted with 10 k pull-ups to VIN, so power VIN from the same voltage as your board's logic (3V3 for ESP32/Pico/Pi).
- Current: about 5 mA idle; each NeoPixel draws up to about 60 mA at full white, so up to about 250 mA with all four at full brightness. Keep brightness low when powered from a 3V3 pin.
- INT is driven by the 3.3 V SAMD09.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x30** by default. Jumpers A0/A1/A2/A3 on the back add 1/2/4/8 (0x30-0x3F, up to 16 boards).
- seesaw protocol: write `[module base, function register]` plus any data. To read, write the two bytes, wait (8 ms in this driver, as in Adafruit's libraries), then read. Big-endian.
- STATUS base 0x00: HW_ID 0x01 reads **0x55** (SAMD09). SWRST 0x7F: write 0xFF, then wait about 500 ms.
- Keys: SWITCHA-SWITCHD are seesaw pins **4, 5, 6, 7** (PA04-PA07) to GND. Set them up with DIRCLR_BULK (0x01 0x03), PULLENSET (0x01 0x0B) and BULK_SET (0x01 0x05), mask 0x000000F0. Read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); a bit reads 0 while its key is pressed. INTENSET (0x01 0x08) with the same mask enables INT.
- NeoPixels: seesaw pin 3, NEOPIXEL base 0x0E. PIN 0x01 = 3, SPEED 0x02 = 1 (800 kHz), BUF_LENGTH 0x03 = 12 (2 bytes), BUF 0x04 = 2-byte offset then GRB bytes, SHOW 0x05.

## Wiring
- ESP32: VIN → 3V3, - → GND, D → D21, C → D22.
- Pico: VIN → 3V3(OUT), - → GND, D → GP4, C → GP5.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VIN → pin 1 (3.3 V), - → pin 6, D → pin 3, C → pin 5.
- Or use a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from neokey1x4 import NeoKey1x4
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
nk = NeoKey1x4(i2c)               # address 0x30
print(nk.keys())                  # [A, B, C, D] True = pressed
nk.pixel(0, 0, 40, 0)             # key A green
```

## Gotchas
- Key A (seesaw pin 4, index 0) is the key at the VIN / "on" LED end of the board.
- Always wait a few ms between the register write and the read, or you get stale bytes.
- In the Sparkbench simulator the four keys are toggles; the NeoPixel colours are accepted but not shown.
- Several boards on one bus: give each its own address with the A0-A3 jumpers.

## Datasheet
- SAMD09 (the chip): https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Atmel-42414-SAM-D09_Datasheet.pdf
- Board guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/neokey-1x4-qt-i2c

from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from neokey1x4 import NeoKey1x4

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
nk = NeoKey1x4(i2c)
while True:
    k = nk.keys()
    for i in range(4):
        nk.pixel(i, 0, 40 if k[i] else 0, 0, show=False)
    nk.show()
    print('keys=%s' % ''.join('1' if p else '0' for p in k))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
